newsitem.title: USA: U.S. adj retail sales off 0.4 pct Sept -- Redbook.
newsitem.headline: U.S. adj retail sales off 0.4 pct Sept -- Redbook.

text.p: U.S. seasonally adjusted retail sales fell 0.4 percent in the five weeks of fiscal September versus August, according to the Lynch, Jones & Ryan Inc Redbook retail sales index.

The index rose 4.8 percent when compared to the same month a year ago, the report said. Adjusted retail sales rose 4.7 percent in the week ended October 5, compared with the same week a year ago, it said.
"Sales came back a little in the fifth and final week but not really enough to save the month," said Jay Meltzer, managing director of Redbook Research, speaking on Reuters Financial Television.
"Some of the retailers tell us finally that the last few days of the month were pretty good and hopefully that will spill over into October," he added.
Meltzer said purchases have been above average in the apparel area, and that soft goods have generally done better than hard goods in nearly every channel of distribution.
He also expressed optimism about the prospects for the Christmas selling season.

"We at Redbook continue to feel we are going to have a Christmas, possibly even a merry Christmas," said Meltzer. "We feel this way despite the well-publicized fact that there will be five fewer shopping days between Thanksgiving and Christmas (compared to last year)."
